title: Windows region capture
summary: Capture a screen region into an editable image using the toolbar or the focused Ctrl+Alt+C shortcut.

Added: Windows region capture is enabled. The editor hides while you drag over a frozen desktop, then opens the selected pixels as a new unsaved image.
Each monitor has its own selection overlay, with one shared selection state and physical screen coordinates.
Verified: Forward capture on the primary display and reverse capture on the negative-coordinate display match all 332800 original fixture pixels, including clipboard transfer and save/reopen.
Escape and right-click restore the previous saved document. Zero-area clicks keep selection open. Unsaved images retain replacement confirmation and its Cancel action.
Fixed: Selector windows expose their titles and normal window metadata to accessibility and window navigation.
Per-monitor overlays avoid the oversized virtual-window input mapping encountered during native verification.

limitations: Verification uses this PC's three-display configuration. Mixed DPI, crossing display boundaries during a drag, display hot-plugging, HDR and other configurations still need qualification.
Ctrl+Alt+C currently requires the editor to be focused. Global capture hotkeys, automatic window selection, scrolling capture and video remain unfinished.
Full interface parity, advanced formatting and library workflows remain incomplete. Capture supports a desktop up to 64 megapixels and a selected image up to 25 megapixels.
The native ClipCraft Save As inspection blocker remains. Capture pixel persistence was checked through the shared engine and clipboard, not that dialog.
